I am 64 years old this year, and I have been farming this flat land in Quzhou County for more than forty years. My family has about 7 mu of good irrigated farmland. My son and daughter-in-law work in the city, so it is mostly me and my wife managing the fields now. At my age, I do not want to take risks with new crops like stevia or chili — those need more labor and the market price is uncertain. I also do not have the strength to manage cotton, which requires too much spraying and pruning.

This year, I will stick to what I know best: the **winter wheat and summer maize rotation**. This is what every household in our village does. The county grain station buys wheat at a stable price, and there is always a market for maize. With this double-cropping system, I can get two harvests from the same piece of land.

For the **winter wheat**, I will sow in early October after rotary tillage. I will use an improved variety like *Jimai 22* or *Luyuan 502* — these are what the seed store recommends and what my neighbors plant. I will spread about 100 kg of compound fertilizer (18-22-5) as basal dressing, and topdress once with urea in the spring. I will irrigate four times: once before winter freeze-up, and three times in spring including the jointing water and grain-filling water. I will spray pesticides three or four times to control aphids and rust. I expect about 1,000 kg per mu if the weather cooperates.

After harvesting the wheat in early June, I will immediately plant **summer maize** using no-tillage direct seeding — there is no time to waste between crops. I will buy hybrid seed, probably *Denghai 605*, because it has good disease resistance and the yield is reliable. I will apply about 100 kg of compound fertilizer (28-6-6) at sowing. Maize here only needs two irrigations, one at the jointing stage and one at the filling stage. I will spray herbicide once and insecticide two or three times. I expect about 1,100 kg per mu.

This plan is simple, uses machinery that I can rent from the village cooperative, and does not require hired labor that I cannot afford. It is the safest choice for an old farmer like me.
